title.latn: Aaj Jaane Ki Zid Na Karo
title.deva: आज जाने की ज़िद न करो

credits.label: Form
credits.note: often sung and listed as a ghazal

intro: “Aaj Jaane Ki Zid Na Karo” is a timeless geet written by Pakistani poet Fayyaz Hashmi and composed by Sohail Rana. Originally popularized by classical vocalist Habib Wali Mohammad in the 1973 Pakistani film Badal Aur Bijli, the song later gained legendary status through ghazal singer Farida Khanum’s rendition in 1993. Sung in Raag Yaman Kalyan, this deeply romantic and melancholic piece expresses a lover’s desperate plea for their beloved to stay a little longer, cherishing fleeting moments of togetherness. Unlike the other pages here, it is a geet: its refrain returns, so repetition is part of the text rather than only of the performance.

deva: यूँ ही पहलू में बैठे रहो

gloss.meaning: side; to sit in someone’s pahlū is to sit close beside them
to be robbed; to be undone

en: Think for a moment, my love
How could I let you go?
It feels like my life fades away
Every time you rise to leave
Grant me just this one wish

gloss.meaning: oath: “I make you swear on yourself”
life of my life, a term of endearment

deva: वक़्त की क़ैद में ज़िन्दगी है मगर
चंद घड़ियां यही हैं जो आज़ाद हैं

en: Life is trapped within time’s grasp
But these few moments are ours
And you’ll long for them forever

deva: कितना मासूम रंगीन है ये समां
हुस्न और इश्क़ की आज मे'राज है
रोक लो आज की रात को

en: The night is innocent and beautiful
A rare meeting of love and desire
Hold onto this night, my love
